x.t: Gukesh starts his world chess title match today
b: Today, a big [[chess|chess]] match begins. India's [[d-gukesh|D Gukesh]] is the world champion. He plays [[javokhir-sindarov|Javokhir Sindarov]] of Uzbekistan.
First, they picked colours in a fun way. Gukesh chose one of two clocks. Each clock held a chocolate chess piece. His piece was dark.
So Sindarov plays White in Game 1, and White moves first. The match is in Switzerland.

o.t: Chocolate knights decide colours as Gukesh and Sindarov begin
b: Game 1 of the World [[chess|Chess]] Championship is being played today, Tuesday 24 November. India's [[d-gukesh|D Gukesh]], the world champion, is defending his title against [[javokhir-sindarov|Javokhir Sindarov]] of Uzbekistan. Both players are 20.

An opening ceremony was held at the United Nations in Geneva on 22 November. In the colour draw, Gukesh picked one of two clocks, each holding a chocolate knight, the chess piece shaped like a horse. His held the dark knight, so Sindarov has the white pieces in Game 1. In chess, White moves first.

The games are at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in [[cologny|Cologny]], Switzerland, overlooking Lake Geneva. Gukesh said: "I don't think I'm here to defend anything, I'm here to win it all over again." There can be up to 14 games, and the first player to reach 7.5 points wins. The match is due to end on 12 December.

stories.think: Gukesh says he is not defending a title but trying to win it again. How might thinking that way help?

quiz.q: What was inside the clocks used to choose the colours?

x.t: Anupama Ramachandran is world snooker champion again
b: India's [[anupama-ramachandran|Anupama Ramachandran]] is the world women's [[snooker|snooker]] champion. She already held the title. Now she has kept it.
Snooker is played on a big table. Players use a long stick to hit coloured balls into pockets.
The final was in [[indore|Indore]], India, on Saturday. Anupama lost the first game. Then she won the next three to take the title.

o.t: Anupama Ramachandran keeps her world snooker title in Indore
b: India's [[anupama-ramachandran|Anupama Ramachandran]] has kept her title at the IBSF World Women's [[snooker|Snooker]] Championship. She beat So Man Yan of Hong Kong 3-1 in the final in [[indore|Indore]], Madhya Pradesh, on Saturday 21 November.

Snooker is a table game. Players use a long stick called a cue to pot, or knock, coloured balls into pockets. A match is split into [[frame|frames]], which are separate games. Anupama lost the first frame, then won the next three to retain, or keep, the title she already held.
"Winning a title is special in itself, but defending it is even more special," she told the news agency PTI. She sealed the win by potting a long blue ball and then the pink one, PTI reported.

stories.think: Why might winning at home feel different from winning far away?

quiz.q: What was the score in the women's final?

x.t: World climate talks end without a final plan
b: Countries met in Antalya, Türkiye, to talk about the climate. The meeting was called [[cop31|COP31]]. It ended on Sunday, two days late.
Every country must agree for a plan to pass. Some countries wanted the plan to name [[fossil-fuels|coal, oil and gas]]. Other countries did not agree.
So there was no final plan. It was the longest meeting of its kind ever.

o.t: COP31 climate talks end in Antalya without a final agreement
b: The United Nations climate talks, [[cop31|COP31]], ended in Antalya, Türkiye, on 22 November without a final agreement. They ran two days longer than planned, making this the longest COP ever.

At these talks, decisions need [[consensus|consensus]]: every country must accept the text. The main split was over [[fossil-fuels|fossil fuels]] such as coal, oil and gas, which the draft text did not mention. Some countries, including the [[european-union|European Union]] (EU), wanted them named; others did not want that. Ireland's climate minister, Darragh O'Brien, spoke for the EU, which rejected the text.

The draft would have said, for the first time, that global warming, the rise in world temperatures, was on course to go past 1.5 degrees Celsius. COP31 President Murat Kurum of Türkiye said there was no consensus. According to Carbon Brief, some other decisions were still adopted, including a global goal on adapting, or getting ready, for a changing climate.

stories.think: If a group decision needs everyone to agree, what could the group do when people disagree?

quiz.q: What was the main disagreement at COP31 about?
a: Which city should host the talks
Whether the text should mention fossil fuels
Which language the talks should use

x.t: Today is Evolution Day, a day about how living things change
b: Today is Evolution Day. On this day in 1859, a famous book came out. Charles Darwin wrote it.
The book explained how each [[species|kind of living thing]] slowly changes. This takes many, many years.
Some living things have features that suit where they live. They tend to have more young. So those features slowly become more common. This is called [[natural-selection|natural selection]].

o.t: Evolution Day marks the 1859 book that changed biology
b: Today, 24 November, is Evolution Day. It is held on this date because [[charles-darwin|Charles Darwin]]'s book On the Origin of Species was published on 24 November 1859. All 1,250 copies of the first printing were ordered by booksellers before publication day, and the book sold out straight away.

The book argued that living things change slowly over many generations (a generation is one step from parents to their young) through [[natural-selection|natural selection]]. Individuals whose features suit their surroundings leave more young, so those features become more common. Darwin used this idea to explain how [[species|species]] change.

Here is a surprise: the word [[evolution|evolution]] does not appear in the main text of the first edition. Only the word evolved appears, in the very last sentence. Today, Darwin's ideas are still central to biology, the science of living things.

stories.think: Think of an animal you know well. Which of its features help it live where it lives?

quiz.q: Why is Evolution Day held on 24 November?
a: On the Origin of Species was published that day in 1859
It is the first day of winter
It is the day the first fossil was found

x.t: Films from 86 countries come to a festival in Goa
b: A big [[film-festival|film festival]] is happening in Goa this week. At a film festival, lots of films are shown to audiences.
This one has more than 150 films from 86 countries. Its big idea is "Stories Without Borders". That means good stories can travel to any country.
One film, called Urum, comes from [[arunachal-pradesh|Arunachal Pradesh]] in India. The festival ends on 28 November.

o.t: India's film festival in Goa shows films from 86 countries
b: The 57th International Film Festival of India, known as IFFI, is being held in [[goa|Goa]] this week. A [[film-festival|film festival]] is an event where many films are screened, or shown, for audiences and filmmakers, often over several days.

This year's theme, the big idea that links the event together, is "Stories Without Borders". The festival is showing more than 150 films from 86 countries, so audiences can see stories from many parts of the world.

Films made in India are part of it too. Urum, a film in the [[nyishi-language|Nyishi language]] from [[arunachal-pradesh|Arunachal Pradesh]], directed by Duyu Tabyo, was chosen for the festival's Indian Panorama section, a part of the programme for selected Indian films. The festival runs until 28 November.

stories.think: If you made a film about where you live, what story would you tell?

quiz.q: How many countries do the festival's films come from?

bigStory.t: Who is the first visitor to China's space station?
bigStory.sub: China's Shenzhou-24 is ready for launch, set to carry Pakistan's first astronaut to Tiangong

x.why: A rocket in China is ready to carry a visitor from Pakistan to China's space station. No one from another country has been there before.

o.why: So far, only Chinese astronauts have been on board Tiangong. This mission is expected to carry the first visitor from another country, an astronaut from Pakistan, for a stay of about a week.

days.o: China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft and its Long March 2F rocket moved to the launch area at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on 17 November. The mission is set to carry Pakistan's first astronaut, the first foreign visitor to Tiangong, China's space station. China has not officially announced the launch date or the crew. The launch has been reported for 25 November.
days.x: A rocket is ready at a launch site in China. It is set to carry a spacecraft called Shenzhou-24. On board will be Pakistan's first astronaut. They will be the first visitor from another country to China's space station.

days.o: Three people are expected to fly: one Pakistani astronaut and two Chinese astronauts. Pakistan has two candidates, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, and it has not been announced which one will fly. The Pakistani astronaut will be a payload specialist, an astronaut whose main job is to carry out experiments. They are expected to stay about one week, then return to Earth with two Chinese astronauts on the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft. China has not officially announced the crew or launch time, but the launch has been reported for 25 November.
days.x: Three astronauts are expected to fly. One is from Pakistan and two are from China. Pakistan has two people who could go. We do not know yet which one will fly. The Pakistani astronaut will do science tests in space. The visitor is expected to stay about one week.

learn.subject: Science
learn.link: From the Evolution Day story: living things slowly change over many generations

b: Living things can slowly change. Charles Darwin wrote about this in a famous book.
The change takes many, many generations. A generation is one step from parents to their young.

Imagine beetles living on dark tree bark. Dark beetles are hard for birds to see. So more dark beetles grow up and have young. Over a long time, most beetles become dark. This is called natural selection.
x.remember: Living things that suit their home have more young, so their features spread.
x.q: In natural selection, which features become more common?

o.t: How does natural selection change living things?
b: Darwin's big idea, natural selection, explains how living things change over very long periods of time. He set it out in his book On the Origin of Species. Darwin's ideas are still central to biology, the science of living things.

Natural selection works slowly, over many generations. A generation is one step from parents to their offspring, meaning their young. Individuals whose features suit their surroundings leave more young, so those features become more common over time.

Imagine a group of beetles living on dark tree bark. Darker beetles are harder for birds to spot, so more of them survive and have young. In this imagined group, darker parents tend to have darker young. After many generations, most beetles in the group could be dark. The example is made up, but it shows how small differences can build up.
o.remember: In natural selection, features that suit the surroundings help individuals leave more young, so those features become more common over generations.
o.q: Why does a feature become more common through natural selection?
a: Individuals with it leave more young
It only lasts for one generation

backThen.t: The fossil skeleton called Lucy is found in Ethiopia
backThen.o: On 24 November 1974, Donald Johanson and Tom Gray found a fossil skeleton at Hadar, in Ethiopia's Awash Valley. It was about 40% of one skeleton, with 47 bones, and about 3.2 million years old. At the time it was the most complete skeleton of a human ancestor ever found. The team named it Lucy at a camp celebration that night, while the Beatles song Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds played.
backThen.x: On this day in 1974, scientists found very old bones in Ethiopia. They came from a human ancestor. She lived about 3.2 million years ago. That night, the team named her Lucy while a Beatles song played.
backThen.why: Lucy's bones showed that human ancestors walked upright on two legs before they had big brains.

hiddenWords.o: Species comes from the Latin word species, which means appearance or kind. It comes from specere, which means to look at. Scientists have used it for groups of living things since about 1600.

Chess comes from the Old French word esches, the plural of eschec, which meant check, or checkmate. The game is named after its key move. Check goes back through Arabic to the Persian word shah, which means king.
